CS10-01.note: Four distinct, internally coherent accounts of the mortar's durability (strengthened / weakened / shielded-then-exposed / inert-but-thick). Each is a claim a real passage could credit; none is incoherent, redundant, or off-register.

CS10-02.note: Identical three-clause frame; only the explanation of the couplet-count disagreement varies (deposition adds / waves strip / counting rule merges / compaction thins). All four are mechanisms that would actually produce a count discrepancy, so none is excludable without the source.

CS10-03.note: A and C are exact inverses of one another and B and D are separate scope limits; all four are legal claims about reader influence on serial publication. Mirrored pairs do not license an elimination because either direction can be the credited one.

CS10-04.note: Considered rejecting D (a dance for a destination the forager has never visited) as self-contradictory, but it is not: swarm-scouting and extrapolated-vector cases exist, and the phrasing does not require the forager to have flown the route. B (recruits misreading the straight run) is the weakest as a 'case' but remains a statable finding.

CS10-05.note: Four purposes for buried gravel (retain fines / store water / frost protection / drain and warm). B and D pull in opposite directions but both are real terrace-engineering rationales; nothing here is decidable from the options alone.

CS10-06.note: Closest call in the batch: C ('a device the poets used to mark speech') and D ('occur more often in passages of direct speech') are the intentional and distributional forms of one proposition, so evidence against either is evidence against the other. That is a uniqueness risk, not an elimination - I cannot say which of the two cannot be the key, so neither is rejected.

rejections.reason: Its own causal clause does not support its claim: cloud traps outgoing heat over the rural reference site as much as over the city, so 'cloud holds a city's heat in' cannot explain a LARGEST value of an urban-minus-rural difference - and the urban heat island is in fact suppressed, not maximised, under overcast skies, so no credible passage would credit this.

CS10-07.note: The rejection is content knowledge about the phenomenon plus an internal defect in the option's reasoning, not a length/hedging tell. C and D are both true of real heat islands, which is a separate uniqueness concern but not an elimination. B is a distinct, real critique (siting of rural stations).

CS10-08.note: A clean permutation of three saga elements over inherited/composed. No option is incoherent and no two are synonyms; the shared halves (A/D share 'inherited legal formulas', B/D share 'composing the disputes') support a 2x2 way of thinking but exclude nothing.

CS10-09.note: Delay, total energy, inferred nickel abundance, reddening rate - four genuine observables of a transient glow, any of which could be the decisive one. Nothing self-refuting or duplicated.

CS10-10.note: Land-rich, experienced, cash-capable, labour-surplus. A and C are both 'better-off households' but name different resources (land vs cash) and a passage can credit one and refute the other, so neither is a near-synonym in the disqualifying sense.

CS10-11.note: All four map to real single-photoreceptor colour-vision mechanisms: layered retinae, chromatic-blur/off-axis pupil (cephalopods), oil droplets (birds), scanning filter (stomatopods). B reads odd on its face but is a published mechanism, so the temptation to reject it as incoherent is exactly the error to avoid.

CS10-12.note: Sealed instruments, per-voyage oral agreement, private ledgers, unwritten custom. B and D are adjacent (both unwritten) but differ on whether terms were negotiated each time or fixed by default, which a passage can distinguish.

CS10-13.note: Four named costs of the thermally tolerant symbiont, each with its own cashing-out clause. B ('reversion cost, being dropped once the warm season ends') is the loosest use of 'cost' but is still a coherent tradeoff claim.

CS10-14.note: Hearth thermal mass, pigment binding, abrasion, fire-lighting - four documented reasons for collecting a mineral. B is mildly self-referential (the mineral acting on a black pigment when it may be one) but works as a mordant/binder claim, so I do not reject it.

CS10-15.note: Four standard assumptions of a competitive labour model (mobility, headcount as the margin of adjustment, many employers, compliance). All are assumptions results could locate a breakdown in.

CS10-16.note: A clean 2x2 of exact opposites (substrates agreed/disagreed, survived/died out). Opposed pairs guarantee that no option is excludable on its face.

CS10-17.note: Amount effect, temperature, continental effect, and post-depositional exposure are all things leaf isotope ratios are argued to record. D is the odd one conceptually (a taphonomic confound rather than a climate signal) but is still a claim about what the ratios record.

CS10-18.note: A entails D (a readership that cannot read the language is a readership other than the buyers), so if A were the key D would also be true - an entailment overlap. But the overlap does not tell me which member is the distractor, so I reject neither. C concerns painters rather than buyers and B concerns reading practice; both stand on their own.
